decks.name: LeetCode #199 - Binary Tree Right Side View
decks.description: Return values of nodes visible from right side of binary tree

cards.question: Binary Tree Right Side View: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the right side of it, return the values of the nodes you can see ordered from top to bottom.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use recursive DFS traversing right subtree before left. Track depth and result array. When visiting a depth for first time, add node value to result (rightmost node at that level). Process right child first to ensure rightmost nodes are visited before left siblings at same level. O(n) time and space for traversing all nodes.

solutions.timeDescription: Linear time as each node is visited exactly once during depth-first traversal
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack proportional to tree height, O(h) typically, O(n) worst case for skewed tree, plus result array
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given tree [1,2,3,null,5,null,4]: dfs(1,0): res=[1]. dfs(3,1): res=[1,3]. dfs(4,2): res=[1,3,4]. dfs(2,1): depth already in res, skip. dfs(5,2): depth already in res, skip. Return [1,3,4] showing nodes visible from right.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS with queue for level-order traversal. For each level, track rightmost non-null node. Process all nodes at current level, updating rightSide variable with each valid node. After processing level, add rightSide value to result. Natural approach for right side view as rightmost node at each level is exactly what we want. O(n) time and space.
